articles.title: 谷歌 DeepMind 发布 AlphaGenome 2 基因序列模型：识别致病变异能力提升近一倍
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 11 日消息，谷歌 DeepMind 发布新一代 DNA 序列模型 AlphaGenome 2，可预测 DNA 序列及其变异对特定人体细胞类型的影响，为科研人员挖掘疾病的细胞驱动因素提供全新工具。人体每个细胞携带相同的 DNA 蓝图，但不同细胞类型会通过开关不同基因完成特定功能。全球的人类细胞图谱项目已对数百万细胞的基因表达进行绘制，但预测细微 DNA 变异如何影响细胞基因表达，仍是尚未解决的难题。此前谷歌已推出初代 AlphaGenome，可预测 DNA 变异对宽泛组织的分子活性影响，并推出了覆盖人类基因组全部 90 亿种单字母变异预测的 AlphaGenome Atlas，助力罕见病、复杂性状与基础生物学研究。AlphaGenome 2 从宽泛组织平均水平缩小至单个细胞类型与状态，并重构了模型架构，变异预测性能实现阶跃式提升，可捕捉宽泛组织模型中遗漏的疾病相关细胞中的变异效应，还能对模型未见过的细胞与疾病状态做出预测。据IT之家了解，相比此前的最优模型，AlphaGenome 2 能识别出近两倍数量的、可改变细胞内基因表达的变异。该模型基于 68 类组织的超过 1 亿个单细胞图谱训练，将静态细胞图谱转化为人类遗传学的预测引擎。目前该模型已通过 AlphaGenome API 面向非商业研究开放，商业研究则处于私密预览阶段。初代 AlphaGenome 可一次性读取百万字母长度的 DNA 序列，同步预测多类组织、数千项实验的相关属性。这种并行方式效率较高，但会分散模型的计算能力，难以捕捉近缘细胞类型之间的细微差异。谷歌对模型处理细胞类型的逻辑进行了根本性重构。AlphaGenome 2 不再采用并行预测模式，而是条件式模型，单次仅针对一种条件（组织、细胞类型或细胞状态）预测 DNA 效应。除百万字母长度的 DNA 序列外，模型在架构的每个阶段都将目标生物条件作为输入，能够学习同一段 DNA 在不同细胞类型中的读取差异。条件式架构还支持跨模态数据填充，可预测缺失的实验数据。模型会将细胞的生物状态与输出结果分离，若科研人员仅输入单细胞基因活性这类单类测量数据，AlphaGenome 2 即可预测染色质可及性等未测量属性，帮助科研人员规划后续实验方向。AlphaGenome 2 同时基于人类与小鼠的组织块、单细胞数据完成训练，纳入了超过 1.07 亿个单细胞图谱。跳出初代模型的组织块平均水平后，该模型可解析心肌、血液免疫细胞等特化细胞内部的活性，挖掘仅在特定细胞类型中发挥作用的关键 DNA 变异。该模型保留了初代模型支持的基因表达、组蛋白修饰、染色质可及性等核心 DNA 功能实验指标，还新增了备受需求的 DNA 甲基化预测能力。AlphaGenome 2 在特定细胞的基因调控预测方面性能显著提升，可帮助科研人员精准定位疾病相关变异。细胞特异性提升：在训练数据未覆盖的基因组区域，AlphaGenome 2 可更好解释同一组织内不同细胞类型间的基因表达差异，能够追踪人体造血干细胞成熟为红细胞、免疫细胞谱系过程中基因表达的连续变化。变异效应预测提升：在覆盖 28 类原代免疫细胞的 TenK10K 大型单细胞数据集测试中，AlphaGenome 2 识别到的因果变异占比达 30%、基因效应方向判断准确率达 43%，相比初代 AlphaGenome 的 16%、23% 接近翻倍，可帮助科研人员发现此前被忽略的候选变异。精准定位疾病相关变异：此前一项里程碑研究发现，一段远端调控序列的变异会通过过度激活肠道免疫巨噬细胞中的 ETS2 基因，诱发炎症性肠病。AlphaGenome 2 在计算层面复现了该结论，精准定位到该因果变异，证明其仅会选择性提升肠道巨噬细胞的 ETS2 基因活性，对其他细胞类型与基因几乎无影响。AlphaGenome 2 无需重新训练，即可泛化到全新的单细胞实验场景。科研人员仅需上传数十个细胞的单细胞 RNA 测序基因活性快照，模型即可将其压缩为细胞状态表征，作为条件输入处理从未见过的细胞状态，性能可媲美甚至超过直接在对应数据集上训练或微调的模型。该能力让 AlphaGenome 2 可预测疾病、疫苗接种等场景下全新细胞状态的变异效应与基因调控规律。例如在针对新冠 mRNA 疫苗的未见过的单细胞数据测试中，AlphaGenome 2 可区分疫苗激活的免疫 T 细胞与静息状态 T 细胞，还揭示了与新冠重症相关的变异，在细胞激活状态下对基因活性的干扰更强 —— articles.title: Xbox 版《GTA 6》预载文件出现 AMD FSR 4.1 线索，首发未必支持
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 11 日消息，数据挖掘者最近一直在研究 Xbox 版《GTA 6》的预载文件，而近期发现的两项线索，让这款游戏的运行表现有了更多值得期待的地方。IT之家注意到，在数据挖掘者 Tex2 分享的文件包中，出现了两个库文件，分别名为 amd_fidelityfx_loader_xbox.dll 和 amd_fidelityfx_upscaler_xbox.dll。这两个文件的名称与微软上周发布的 FSR 4.1 Xbox GDK 示例项目中的相关术语一致。当然，这并不意味着 AMD 的 FSR 4.1 技术一定会在《GTA 6》发售时，或者在游戏推出后加入其中。不过，至少可以确认，游戏存在采用最新超分辨率技术的可能性。FSR 4 是 AMD 超分辨率技术的一次重大升级，将此前以传统算法为主的方案转向了机器学习技术。与过去依赖空间和时间算法不同，新版本开始利用神经网络进行图像重建。FSR 4 能够提供更加清晰的画面，同时减少画面拖影、闪烁和各种视觉瑕疵，代价则是会占用少量额外的 GPU 计算资源。微软和 AMD 已于 11 月 5 日向 Xbox 开发者推出 FSR 4.1，时间上比该技术通过测试版驱动登陆 Xbox Ally 掌机晚了大约两周。与 NVIDIA DLSS、Intel XeSS 等竞争方案相比，AMD FSR 正在迅速缩小差距。大多数玩家仍然将 DLSS 视为 AI 超分辨率技术的标杆，但 AMD 技术广泛的硬件兼容性同样不容忽视。对于游戏主机而言，FSR 更是目前唯一可用的选择，而 4.1 版本相较此前的 FSR 已经实现了相当明显的升级。不过，目前还不能断言《GTA 6》首发时就会支持 FSR 4.1。数据挖掘发现的相关文件确实说明这种可能性存在，但文件出现在游戏中，并不能证明开发团队已经完成了实际集成。开发商 Rockstar 至今没有对此发表任何评论。按理说，面对近期 PS5 公布的 PSSR 超分辨率技术相关消息，Xbox 方面应该也有动力尽快公布类似的技术进展。目前最大的问题在于时间安排。除非 Rockstar 在开发过程中提前获得了 FSR 4.1 的使用权限，否则，要在距离 11 月 19 日发售仅剩几天的情况下，完成针对游戏的超分辨率技术适配，似乎并不现实。Xbox 版《GTA 6》更可能会在发售后才加入 FSR 4.1 支持。目前看来，相关技术准备工作似乎已经具备一定基础，而 Rockstar 显然有充分的动力，让这款游戏尽可能流畅地运行在逐渐老旧的主机硬件上。这一点对于 Xbox Series S 尤其重要。由于该机型的硬件性能相对有限，任何能够减轻渲染压力的技术，都能带来不小的帮助。选择在游戏发售后再加入这项技术，也能降低对首发版本造成影响的风险。对于这种情况来说，晚一点总比没有好。总而言之，如果 Xbox 版《GTA 6》首发时没有支持 FSR 4.1，玩家也不必太过失望。这项技术从来没有得到官方确认，后续通过更新加入的可能性反而更大。毕竟，很难想象《GTA 6》这样一款具有世代意义的游戏，会错过展示 AMD 最新超分辨率技术的绝佳机会。

articles.title: 保时捷 CEO 骆明楷批评特斯拉 Roadster 发布会：我们不想搞任何特效或表演
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 11 日消息，据彭博社今天（11 日）晚间报道，保时捷 CEO 骆明楷（Michael Leiters）批评特斯拉 Roadster 发布会过于追求噱头，并指出特斯拉展示的飞行汽车与保时捷 Mission S 概念车面向不同的消费群体。骆明楷在柏林出席一场会议时直言：“我们不想搞任何特效或表演。”同时，他强调，保时捷希望通过新车展示真正的技术创新。特斯拉与保时捷都在当地时间 10 月 15 日（IT之家注：北京时间均为 16 日上午）发布新车，但两场活动的风格截然不同。特斯拉主打炫目的展示效果，配备压缩空气推进器的 Roadster 从斜坡腾空跃起，在空中翻转后稳稳落地。骆明楷称，全新的中置发动机超跑 Mission S 发布以来获得了客户“极其热烈”的反响。作为保时捷进一步向高端市场发展的核心车型，该车定位高于 911，预计售价也将高出不少，并兼容混动和纯燃油动力。如果 Mission S 最终量产，保时捷将自 918 Spyder 以来首次重返法拉利占据主导地位的超级跑车市场。保时捷希望凭借更高的稀缺性和售价，推动利润率回升。不过，另一家“超跑俱乐部”成员法拉利的 CEO 贝内代托 · 维尼亚，却给特斯拉 Roadster 发布会的技术表现和展示效果都打了 10 分满分。“这说明汽车行业还有很大的创新空间。我们必须继续怀揣梦想。作为欧洲人，我要感谢你们，让我们看到，即使在传统行业，也依然能够创新，敢于大胆尝试。”

articles.title: 以旧换新 3999 → 2291 元：小米米家智能净烟机 3 Pro 国补直降，7 级大风力
articles.content: 【京东活动可能随时变更，需以实付款为准】小米 · 米家智能净烟机 3 Pro 开售于 2026 年 8 月，官方定价 3999 元。京东 11.11 大促期间，按下方步骤下单，叠加 PLUS 立减 + 15% 国补后仅需 2291 元：领 8.7 折券：点此查看。下单时选择“以旧换新 → 个护健康 → 普通牙刷（无需回收）”补贴 200 元。参与“多买多返”活动返 30 元 E 卡，晒单返 50 元京豆，社交平台种草返 50 元京豆（详询客服）京东小米 米家智能净烟机 3 ProMJ06A 以旧换新后 2291 元直达链接京东 11.11 无门槛红包至高 26888 元，支持即领即用，下单直接当钱花：点此抽取。米家智能净烟机 3 Pro 主打三重净烟专利，可净吸油烟气味、PM2.5，包含防逸阻隔气帘拦截余烟、高速后倾气流瞬吸浓烟、四涡捕集气旋源头锁烟三个技术点。经测试，爆炒前后本产品 PM2.5 平均波动约 4μg/m³，其他传统油烟机约 89μg/m³，净烟效果获得国际实验室莱茵 TÜV 净烟效果验证。该产品支持 7 级强风大吸力，搭载 360W 高速电机，配合自动巡航算法，最高风速可达 16m/s ，最大静压 1600Pa ，瞬吸浓烟速度更快，防止油烟倒灌。这款产品搭载创新防逸气帘，烟机顶部内置双贯流风机，形成向下匀速风幕，能够有效拦截顶部跑烟，避免油烟直扑口鼻。米家智能净烟机 3Pro 进行了 15 处降噪优化，包含 5 大核心技术 + 10 项降噪设计，多维度优化后高挡风力噪音仅 60dB(A) ，声强降低 60%。它还配备专利离子抑菌技术，通过专利离子净化模块释放高浓度负离子，可降低 PM2.5 微粒、空气微尘浓度，抑制细菌滋生，PM2.5 去除率可达 97% ，除菌率可达 95%。该产品支持全厨空气监测，可实现 24 小时燃气、烟雾监测，有害气体超标时主动预警，并可联动烟机自动换气，时刻守护家人安全；还搭载微米级空气监测仪，支持 PM2.5 实时显示，采用三色色数显示，绿色代表 PM2.5 低值、橙色代表中值、红色代表高值，状态一目了然。清洁方面，米家智能净烟机 3 Pro 前导烟面板采用纳米晶格工艺，形成疏水疏油保护层，油污水滴不易残留，轻松擦净厨后油污；内部内置免拆洗风机，叶轮采用疏油涂层从根源抗油防污，搭配离心风膜技术高速甩离油污，实现风机免拆洗，还新增自清洁模式，可一键省心清洁。设计方面，该产品采用精致星辰银外观，轻奢配色亲肤面板触感柔和，可适配多种家居风格；采用顶吸形态不挡锅，可容纳多层大蒸锅；配备 29 英寸柔光大灯，提供均匀照明让烹饪视野清晰；搭载高清灵动彩屏，下厨信息抬头即可看见；还支持手势控制，开关、调速不沾油污。智能方面，米家智能净烟机 3 Pro 支持小米澎湃智联，支持小爱音箱语音控制、米家 APP 自定义控制，还能联动多种米家智能设备，支持烟灶联动（需搭配 2021 年后上市的米家灶具），可实现开火自动排烟，畅享智能厨房新体验。IT之家附详细参数如下：京东小米 米家智能净烟机 3 ProMJ06A 以旧换新后 2291 元直达链接淘宝 11.11 主会场：点此前往京东 11.11 主会场：点此前往京东 11.11 手机叠加国补立减千元：点此查看京东 11.11 家电家居主会场：点此前往京东 11.11 数码主会场：点此前往

articles.title: 俄罗斯月球核电站新计划：明年选定方案、本世纪 30 年代中期运行
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 11 日消息，据央视新闻报道，当地时间 10 日，俄罗斯国家原子能公司首席执行官利哈乔夫表示，该公司计划于 2027 年选定月球核电站方案。利哈乔夫在当日举行的政府航天发展战略会议后透露，俄罗斯国家原子能公司正在研究 5 种月球核电站方案，将于 2027 年选定其中一种。当前，国家原子能公司、俄罗斯库尔恰托夫研究所与俄罗斯科学院正在联合研究相关课题。他进一步表示：“这里说的是功率可达 10 千瓦的月球核电站，计划于 21 世纪 30 年代中期开始运行。目前我们正在深入研究 5 种构型，从把核能直接转换为电能，到建造相应的涡轮装置。我们必须在明年选定构型并启动相关工作。”参与俄罗斯月球发电站项目的俄库尔恰托夫研究所所长米哈伊尔 · 科瓦尔丘克今年 3 月表示，俄罗斯可能在 5 至 7 年内在月球上建成核电站。据IT之家此前报道，去年 12 月，俄罗斯国家航天集团宣布与拉沃奇金科研生产联合体签署了一项合同，希望在 2036 年前建成一座月球发电站，合同于同年开始执行。当时，俄罗斯国家航天集团强调：“该项目是朝着建立永久运行的月球科研站，并从一次性任务过渡到长期月球探测计划迈出的重要一步。”相关阅读：《俄罗斯计划 2036 年前建成月球发电站，开启长期月球探测计划》

articles.title: Adobe 公布四项 AI 实验项目：照片秒变 3D 场景，还能通过聊天设计 AI 角色
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 11 日消息，每年举办的 Adobe MAX 大会上，Adobe 展示的最令人印象深刻的技术之一，往往是那些仍处于实验阶段、尚未正式推出的创新功能。今天，该公司公布了最新一批实验项目：它们能够将普通图片转换为可探索的 3D 场景，通过与 AI 角色对话来设计角色形象，还能让照片编辑变成简单的复制粘贴操作。首先是非常奇特的 Project Screen Test 项目，其旨在让用户更轻松地创建 AI 生成角色，并将其应用于视频内容。IT之家注意到，与传统方式不同，用户不再只是通过文字提示词描述角色应该如何说话、如何表现，而是可以直接与角色对话，在类似演员试镜的环境中对其进行指导。使用时，用户首先需要描述角色的一些基本性格特征，例如“焦虑、害羞、笨拙”等，并为角色设置声音。声音可以从预设选项中选择，也可以通过文字提示词描述，或者上传一段音频样本，让 AI 以此为参考。随后，用户可以像通过 FaceTime 与人视频通话一样，与 AI 角色展开对话，进一步完善其人物设定，包括成长背景、性格、目标、缺点、恐惧，以及一些独特的动作习惯等。完成角色设计后，用户还可以描述希望角色置身其中的环境或情景，生成相应的动态试镜视频。目前，Project Screen Test 仍然是一项独立的创意实验，尚不清楚其未来是否会被整合进 Adobe 现有的 AI 视频工具中。从实际效果来看，与许多缺乏灵魂的 AI 动画角色相比，这项工具生成的角色拥有更加鲜明、连贯的个性。不过，这恰恰也是它存在的意义：与传统动画制作相比，AI 视频生成能够提供的创作控制权要少得多。在传统动画中，角色的每一个细节都经过创作者有意识的设计，而 AI 生成的角色很难做到这一点。另一个项目是 Project Sight Span，它能够将普通照片和图片转换为可供用户探索的 3D 空间，从而重新调整画面的构图和视角。这项技术可以生成原始画面之外的物体和背景，将一张平面图片扩展成完整的三维环境。即使用户转动视角，查看原本被拍摄者遮挡的背后区域，系统生成的内容也能与原始画面自然衔接。不过，在 3D 环境中浏览时，画面中的物体和背景会显得像素化，细节也不够清晰。但当用户选定最终视角后，系统便会恢复相应画面的分辨率。Sight Span 支持各种平面图像，包括照片、绘画和插画，同时能够保留并复现原作品的艺术风格。即使用户调整照片中人物的纹身位置或面部特征，这些细节依然能够令人惊讶地保持辨识度，并与原始参考图像高度一致。这项技术有点像苹果 Spatial Reframing 空间重构功能的强化版：用户不仅可以更加大幅度地调整画面中的元素，甚至能够彻底改变拍摄角度。不过，经过如此大幅度调整后，最终作品似乎也已经不太适合继续称为一张照片了。Project Sound Bender 则是一项 AI 音频混音功能，用户可以像在色轮上移动光标一样，自由调整视频中的音效。使用时，用户只需上传一段视频，并通过文字提示词描述想要的声音效果，例如“冒着气泡的科幻炼金锅声音”。Sound Bender 随后会自动生成相应音效，并将其与视频同步。与此同时，工具还会提供一个方形声音控制面板，让用户实时调整音效。面板的四个角会自动分配不同类型的 AI 生成声音，例如密集的咕噜声和气泡爆裂声、岩石沸腾般的轰鸣声、带有音高变化的电子音，以及噼啪作响的电火花声。用户可以在面板上拖动光标，自由选择希望突出的声音类型，也可以分别为四个角设置不同的音效。Adobe 展示的第四个项目是 Project Rinse Repeat，它能够让用户复制已经完成的编辑操作，并自动将相同的处理效果应用到同一张照片中的其他人物或物体上。例如，用户花费大量时间为照片中的某个人物进行磨皮，去除痘痘和皮肤瑕疵后，Rinse Repeat 就可以根据用户已经完成的具体修改，自动将类似处理应用到合影中的其他人物身上。这项功能也可以用于商业营销图片。例如，用户可以为产品添加阴影效果，即使其他产品的形状和尺寸不同，系统也能自动适配相应的阴影。Rinse Repeat 基于 Photoshop 构建。值得注意的是，应用到其他人物或物体上的编辑效果仍然完全可编辑，因为工具会调用 Photoshop 原生功能重新创建这些修改，而不是简单地将处理后的图像覆盖上去。需要注意的是，这些名为“Sneaks”的项目目前都只是技术预览，未来有可能被开发成 Adobe Creative Cloud 应用或 Firefly 平台中的正式工具，但并不保证所有项目最终都会推出。不过，这些项目几乎全部围绕 Adobe 的生成式 AI 技术展开。考虑到 AI 工具如今已经成为 Adobe 增长战略的核心，至少有一部分实验功能最终正式上线的可能性相当高。无论这些 AI

articles.title: 贴脸开大：当着 XBOX 高层的面，前《铁拳》总监原田胜弘直言希望别再推出 XSS 这样的主机
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 11 日消息，前《铁拳》系列总监、现任 VS Studio CEO 原田胜弘向来说话毫不客气。最近，他又在一场开发者座谈会上当着 XBOX 团队成员的面直言，希望微软别再推出 XBOX Series S 这样的主机。当地时间 9 日，据外媒 Inven Global 报道，原田胜弘出席了在韩国举行的 2026 年主机游戏开发者大会。座谈会由前索尼总裁吉田修平主持，参与讨论的还有《剑星》开发商 Shift Up CTO 李东基、《弹丸论破》开发商 Too Kyo Games CEO 小高和刚、《赛博朋克 2077》开发商 CD Projekt RED 游戏副总监帕维尔 · 萨斯科，以及《边缘世界》开发商 Ludeon Studios CEO 泰南 · 西尔维斯特。讨论围绕主机游戏开发的优势，以及开发者适配不同平台时遇到的难题展开。原田胜弘率先谈起主机对格斗游戏的好处，认为主机硬件尤其适合举办格斗游戏比赛和电竞赛事。随后，原田胜弘把话题转向了自己不太满意的 XBOX Series S。“不过，趁现在有机会，我有件事特别想说。正好今天有 XBOX 高层在现场，我真希望微软别再推出 XBOX Series S 这样的主机了。”他还当面问萨斯科，开发游戏时是不是也被 Series S 气得不轻。萨斯科听完忍不住大笑，随后回答：“它总是给我们出难题，逼着我们把代码优化得非常精细。”原田胜弘随即调侃道：你刚才说得那么客气，其实就是想说‘XBOX Series S 烂透了’，对吧？内存小是一回事，最麻烦的是，它和 Series X 看起来几乎一样，性能却差了一截。如果要把游戏移植到任天堂 Switch 2，开发者还能换个思路，告诉自己‘Switch 2 是面向任天堂玩家的另一种设备！’但 XBOX 就不一样了。好不容易把游戏做到最好，结果还得给一个性能稍差的孩子再做一遍，感觉就是这样。更麻烦的是，在美国等市场，Series S 的用户甚至比 Series X 还多，我们根本不能随便应付。可游戏发售以后，Series S 玩家却不去找微软，而是跑来质问开发者：‘凭什么只有 Series S 版的贴图分辨率这么低？’萨斯科随后也谈到了 Series S 的好处。他承认，很多玩家不了解 Series S 性能限制背后的技术原因，但针对低性能硬件进行优化，往往也能让游戏在其他平台上运行得更流畅。IT之家获悉，他举例称，《赛博朋克 2077》开发团队将移植 Switch 2 版时积累的优化成果应用到其他平台后，效果相当明显。此外，Series S 价格较低，也能帮助游戏行业吸引更多玩家、扩大市场。原田胜弘听后又开起了玩笑：“帕维尔总监把 Series S 夸得这么委婉，台下那位微软代表都一个劲儿地点头。我都担心他们听完觉得没问题，结果下一代 XBOX 又给我们弄出个‘Helix S’来。”最后，Shift Up CTO 李东基表达了对微软下一代主机的期待：“我个人很期待下一代 XBOX‘Helix’。从工程师的角度来说，如果你们能尽早让韩国开发者率先拿到开发机，我们一定会全力投入开发。”

articles.content: JioHotstar evaluated 6 approaches to code retrieval for AI coding agents using SWE, CodeScale Bench, and an internal question-answering harness. articles.title: 路虎卫士新增 6 款 Atlas 系列车漆，灵感来自世界各地自然景观
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 11 日消息，据外媒 motor1 报道，当地时间 10 日，路虎卫士宣布新增 6 款 Atlas 系列车漆，灵感来自世界各地的自然景观，分别借鉴肯尼亚西南部的草原、意大利火山岛、爱尔兰、英格兰湖区，以及澳大利亚蓝山地区的地下洞穴。六款车漆中，“马拉红”和“潘泰莱里亚蓝”由卫士昔日的经典颜色重新设计而来，“戈尔韦绿”和“白金汉蓝”则属于经典配色回归，“艾拉绿”和“杰诺兰金”是首次亮相。马拉红以肯尼亚马赛人的聚居地区为灵感，是经典马赛红的重新演绎。潘泰莱里亚蓝取材于西西里岛附近的潘泰莱里亚火山岛，基于经典盛典蓝重新设计。戈尔韦绿得名于爱尔兰戈尔韦郡。白金汉蓝则是经典车漆直接回归，曾在 2006 年至 2013 年间用于旧款卫士车型。两款配色并不限于 OCTA 车型，也可供其他版本选择。艾拉绿和杰诺兰金是此次新增的两款全新颜色，分别以英格兰湖区的艾拉瀑布和澳大利亚蓝山地下的杰诺兰石灰岩洞穴为灵感。六款车漆均搭配黑色撞色车顶，部分卫士 90 和 110 车型还可选装白色车顶，具体取决于车型配置和销售市场。据IT之家了解，卫士目前提供 90、110 和 130 三种车身版本，其中 130 采用三排座椅布局，最多可乘坐八人。Atlas 系列车漆覆盖部分卫士 90、110 和 130 车型，较新的 Vertex 版、X 版和 OCTA 高性能版同样支持，具体可选颜色仍因配置和销售地区而异。此外，部分车型无法选装 Atlas 系列车漆：卫士 S 版、硬顶商用 S 版、130 Outbound 版、奖杯特别版，以及中东和北非市场的 525 Ultimate 特别版、中国市场的黑色外观特别版。

articles.title: DeepL 推出旗下最逼真语音 AI 翻译模型 Aure，实时复现说话者语气起伏、情绪流转等
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 11 日消息，当地时间 11 月 11 日，DeepL 推出语音 AI 翻译模型 Aure，官方称这是其迄今最具动态感、表现最逼真的语音 AI（Voice AI）模型，不过该模型暂不支持中文。据介绍，作为 DeepL Voice 的底层驱动核心，Aure 能够持续动态适配翻译语音，实时复现说话者的语气起伏、情绪流转、重音强调及语速快慢。使得语音翻译不仅局限于传递字面词句，更能完整保留赋予人类对话自然度与感染力的个性特色、细腻情感及丰富表达。官方表示，Aure 建立在 DeepL 近期推出的声音保留技术基础之上。该技术使人们能够以自己辨识度极高的原声音色跨语言交流，摆脱了千篇一律的机械合成音。如果说这一突破成功保留了说话者的音色特征，那么 Aure 则更进一步：它能全程捕捉声音在对话中的动态起伏与即时反应，将人类自然言语中更多的自发性与真实神韵注入实时翻译中。Aure 已支持 DeepL Voice 网页会议版、DeepL Voice 面对面交谈版以及 DeepL 语音 API。该模型首发支持英语、德语、西班牙语、法语、意大利语、日语、葡萄牙语及韩语，后续将逐步拓展至更多语种。对于 Aure 尚未支持的语言，DeepL Voice 会自动使用之前的语音模型。IT之家附官网链接：https://www.deepl.com/zh/products/voice/aure

articles.title: 马斯克旗下 Grok 被指生成儿童色情图像，xAI 面临多起集体诉讼
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 11 日消息，据彭博社报道，简 · 多伊（Jane Doe）已经多年没有想起过自己的初中毕业典礼，直到一名执法调查人员拿出当年庆祝活动的一张照片，开始向她询问相关情况。照片中的她当时只有 14 岁，身穿黄色碎花连衣裙，面带笑容，双臂搭在几名朋友的肩膀上。其中一些朋友，她如今已经很少联系。调查人员告诉她，照片中一名同学的成年哥哥，曾利用埃隆 · 马斯克（Elon Musk）旗下的人工智能聊天机器人 Grok，将这张原本再普通不过的照片篡改成儿童性虐待材料（CSAM）。生成的图片中，正值初二年级的简 · 多伊全身赤裸，以性挑逗姿势出现。这些图片随后被发布到了互联网上。她在针对马斯克旗下生成式 AI 公司、Grok 开发商 xAI 提起的一起集体诉讼中，以简 · 多伊 5 号的身份参与案件。简 · 多伊 5 号在一份诉状中写道：“目前根本无法确定，还有多少其他儿童性犯罪者可能已经持有简 · 多伊 5 号的儿童性虐待图片，也无法确定这些图片通过暗网渠道和应用程序在网上传播的范围究竟有多广。”现年 18 岁的简 · 多伊在即将离开家乡前往大学就读的几天前接受采访时表示：“这些图片已经流传出去了，我真的无能为力。这才是最让我害怕的事情。”她还说：“这件事让我觉得，自己好像想要放弃一切。”如今，借助 AI，任何人都可以轻而易举地从个人社交媒体账号或学校网站上获取普通照片，并在几秒钟内将其变成令人难以想象的色情图像。简 · 多伊 5 号只是越来越多试图通过法律手段追究 xAI 责任的年轻受害者之一，她们认为 Grok 帮助用户制作了这些令人不安的图片。在此过程中，她们面对的不仅是一家由全球首富支持的公司，还涉及 AI 时代一个至今尚无定论的根本性问题：当聊天机器人生成侵害他人的内容时，最终应该由谁承担法律责任？是向 AI 发出指令的用户，还是开发这项技术的公司？抑或双方都应承担责任？xAI 表示，与 OpenAI、Anthropic 公司和 Meta 公司等竞争对手一样，该公司严格禁止用户利用聊天机器人制作此类图像，并采取了技术措施防止用户生成相关内容。这类问题如今已经成为整个 AI 行业面临的普遍难题。然而，自 2023 年 Grok 发布以来，马斯克一直有意将其塑造成一款比竞争对手限制更少、更具争议性的产品。他曾鼓励用户利用聊天机器人生成色情 AI 内容。Grok 专门推出了名为“Spicy”的模式，主打“更加大胆、视觉表现更具冲击力的叙事”，支持生成不适合在工作场所观看（NSFW）的图片和视频。xAI 曾表示，“Spicy”和“Unhinged”两种模式符合 Grok 追求“最大程度求真”的产品目标。“这些图片已经流传出去了，我真的无能为力。”专家认为，这种产品定位让 Grok 在那些希望突破互联网规则的用户群体中尤其受欢迎。今年早些时候，X 平台上的用户一度利用 Grok 每小时生成数千张带有性暗示或将人物衣物移除的图片。一项第三方分析发现，Grok 生成的视觉内容中，绝大多数都属于这一类型。其他调查还发现，其中许多图片似乎涉及未成年人。有报告估计，Grok 曾允许用户生成数万张逼真的儿童性化图片。X 平台上此类内容大量出现，引发了全球范围内的强烈反弹。迫于舆论压力，X 于今年 1 月将 Grok 的图片生成功能改为付费用户专享。但批评人士认为，这一举措不过是将一项饱受争议的功能变成了令人趋之若鹜的付费产品。马斯克则将露骨色情内容的产生归咎于 Grok 的用户，而不是产品本身。今年 1 月，他曾表示，自己“没有听说过任何涉及未成年人的裸露图片”。xAI 随后也表示，已经关闭 Grok 为任何真实人物生成未经同意的性化图片的能力。对于本文的采访请求，xAI 以相关诉讼尚未结束为由拒绝置评。今年春季，xAI 美洲地区全球政府事务负责人威尔弗雷多 · 费尔南德斯（Wifredo Fernández）曾表示：“xAI 对儿童性剥削行为采取零容忍态度，我们决心让自己的产品成为那些企图侵害未成年人的人无法利用的工具。”今年 9 月，X 表示，会将此类内容报告给非营利组织美国国家失踪与受虐儿童中心（NCMEC），由该机构将相关线索转交执法部门。过去几个月，xAI 还起诉了多名涉嫌滥用 Grok、危害儿童安全的个人。但与此同时，该公司也在积极挑战旨在保护公众免受未经同意的 AI 色情图像侵害的法律。今年夏天，xAI 起诉美国明尼苏达州，反对该州一项针对 AI 公司利用技术将人物照片处理成裸体图像的法律。根据该州法律，允许用户进行此类图像处理的 AI 公司可能受到处罚。xAI 在诉讼文件中辩称，这项法律违反了美国宪法第一修正案，因为其适用范围“远远超出了立法目标本身，使大量受到宪法保护的言论也面临民事责任和政府制裁”。今年 10 月

articles.title: AI 提升飓风预报精度，人类气象专家仍不可替代
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 11 日消息，人工智能经常因为数据中心能耗巨大而受到批评。数据中心对电力的庞大需求推动了化石燃料的使用，也进一步加剧了气候变化。但与此同时，AI 也正在帮助气象学家显著提高天气预报的准确性，其中就包括飓风预测。这类天气系统以预测难度极高著称，而在全球变暖的背景下，飓风带来的威胁也日益加剧。据 Techxplore 报道，美国国家飓风中心（NHC）去年开始使用谷歌 DeepMind 的 AI 模型，目前正与该公司合作开发下一代模型。今年，这项技术的价值进一步凸显。受强厄尔尼诺天气模式影响，太平洋地区出现了创纪录数量的飓风；上个月，飓风伊萨亚斯（Isaias）也以强风暴的形式袭击了美国东南部。负责 DeepMind 气旋研究工作的研究科学家费兰 · 阿莱特（Ferran Alet）解释称，谷歌并没有专门针对飓风开发独立模型，而是使用与日常天气预报相同的模型，只不过将其能力推向了极限。他在接受法新社采访时表示：“我们认为，极端天气几乎是我们应该努力攻克的目标，因为它是最具挑战性的领域。只要解决了这个难题，其他问题也就迎刃而解。”在引入 AI 之前，美国国家飓风中心主要使用几类模型预测热带气旋。其中，动力学模型依靠超级计算机求解控制大气运动的流体力学和热力学方程；统计模型则根据历史数据，分析风暴行为与地理位置、日期等变量之间的关系；混合模型则将物理学原理与统计方法结合起来。相比之下，AI 模型同样通过海量数据集进行学习，但规模要大得多，也能够识别复杂程度更高的规律。预报时间更长，预测精度更高IT之家注意到，DeepMind 今年 8 月发表在《自然》（Nature）杂志上的一项研究显示，该模型平均可以让气象预报提前一天达到原有模型的预测准确度。换句话说，过去需要提前两天才能达到的预报精度，现在可以提前三天实现。在预测飓风伊萨亚斯时，DeepMind 的模型甚至在风暴正式形成前整整一周，就识别出它可能发展为热带气旋。该模型还能够针对每个气旋生成 1000 种可能的发展情景，并同时预测降雨情况、风暴路径和强度，也就是风暴将沿着什么路线移动，以及最终可能达到多强的程度。美国国家飓风中心业务部门负责人丹 · 布朗（Dan Brown）介绍称：“NHC 于 2025 年 6 月下旬开始在实际业务中使用 AI 模型。2026 年，谷歌 DeepMind 的模型也被纳入 NHC 的部分路径和强度综合预测辅助系统。”目前，NHC 还在使用欧洲中期天气预报中心和美国国家气象局开发的 AI 模型，并已与谷歌达成合作协议，共同推进相关模型的研发。布朗表示，在预测伊萨亚斯时，AI 模型在风暴路径方面表现相当出色。他还指出：“AI 模型似乎特别擅长快速预测复杂引导气流模式的变化。”人类专家仍然不可或缺布朗特别提到了 DeepMind 的模型，以及 NHC 自主开发的 HCCA 模型，认为它们是目前在飓风路径和强度预测方面表现最出色的辅助工具之一。不过，这项技术并非没有局限性。布朗指出，单个模型在不同预测周期之间，可能会突然大幅调整对飓风路径或强度的判断。因此，飓风专家仍然需要依靠自身经验和专业判断，确定哪些模型最能反映特定风暴的实际情况，再将不同模型的预测结果综合起来。他还强调，AI 模型的训练基础实际上来自传统物理模型建立的数据和预测体系。布朗表示：“对于飓风专家来说，他们的重要性反而比以往任何时候都更高。算法可以给出风暴路径的概率预测，但它无法像专家那样，结合实时飞机观测数据和卫星数据，判断风暴当前的实际结构。”AI 提高飓风预测精度的同时，美国数据中心建设热潮也正在迅速改变电力供应结构。Cleanview 的一项分析显示，计划中的新一代数据中心将主要依靠天然气供电，这将增加美国的碳排放，加剧气候变化。而气候变化反过来也在改变飓风的表现：飓风正在变得更加强劲，携带的降雨量更多，移动速度也更慢，最终导致其造成的破坏进一步加剧。

articles.title: 高铁座椅 USB 充电口“越充越掉电”，12306 客服称仅作应急补电使用
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 11 日消息，近日有网友发帖称，高铁座椅 USB 接口给手机充电越充越掉电，一时间“乘客称高铁座椅充电越充越掉电”话题引发热议。11 月 10 日，“万维视频”就此事致电铁路 12306 官方热线。接线客服回应称，列车充电口的电压低于家里使用的交流电电压，是用来应急补电用的，如果手机电量较少或平时手机用电习惯较差的旅客，还是建议随身携带充电宝。IT之家同时也提醒大家，客流高峰时段可能出现充电资源紧张情况，建议在出行前确保电子设备电量充足，最好是携带备用的移动电源。此外，市场监管总局 5 月 25 日修订并发布新版《强制性产品认证实施规则移动电源、锂离子电池和电池组》。今年 9 月，有关认证机构已按新版规则发出首批 32 张 3C 认证证书。按照新版规则获得 3C 认证的移动电源，必须具备智能管理、电压调节和异常禁用等功能，安全性能显著提升。

Abstract: Closed-loop autonomous experimentation can accelerate scientific discovery, but implementation effort limits accessibility. articles.title: EarthRecord: From Pixels to Land Change with Multimodal Agents over Four Decades of Satellite Imagery
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12934v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: While multimodal agents now carry out complex data analysis with tools, their ability to turn decades of satellite imagery into reliable land-change analysis, crucial for Earth observation science, remains unmeasured. Existing benchmarks fall short: they pose questions on curated images or give agents preprocessed inputs, leaving out the raw multi-sensor archives where such analysis begins. We introduce EarthRecord, a benchmark built on the raw record of 56 sites: four decades of Landsat, MODIS, VIIRS, and Sentinel-2 data, with cloud masking and cross-sensor harmonization left to the agent. It poses 238 land-change questions across ten analysis tasks, scored against withheld references from global products, agreement among methods, and visual interpretation. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12935v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Topic monitoring is the task of labelling the topic of each token in a model's response during generation. Activation-based monitors that run at generation time have so far been trained to detect harmful content and are limited to two or three classes. We introduce TopicScope, a framework for training causal topic classifiers on SAE features that assign a topic to every token, so that the label can change partway through a response. We train three detector architectures on synthetic multi-topic conversations covering seven topics. Across Gemma-3 1B and 4B, monitors trained on features extracted from prefill hidden states were able to generalise to decoding. articles.content:

Abstract: We study when and how multimodal input improves knowledge graph question answering (KGQA) in large vision--language models. Abstract: The rapid proliferation of autonomously acting AI agents makes the governance of agentic systems urgent. arXiv:2611.12950v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Black-box LLM fingerprinting aims to determine whether a target model was derived from a source model when only the output responses to input queries are observable. One way to reveal this relationship is to perturb each query and observe the resulting responses of both models, yielding two corresponding sets of response variations. These sets provide two complementary sources of information: the relations among response changes within each set, and the correspondence of response changes between the two sets. Abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have enabled weight-space programming (WSP), which directly generates neural network weights without gradient-based optimization. Abstract: Recent advances in large models have accelerated AI for Science toward agentic science, where AI agents autonomously conduct scientific discovery. Realising this vision requires closing the loop between computational reasoning and physical experimentation, positioning self-driving laboratories (SDLs) as critical enablers. By treating models as disembodied planners that output symbolic workflows for separate robotic systems, current architectures inherently block the development of embodied experimental intuition. Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can generate SQL and SQL--Python workflows for investment research, but ensuring point-in-time (PIT) validity remains challenging. Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) show strong potential for social media content moderation, but their trustworthiness beyond overall accuracy remains underexplored. Evaluating 16 open-weight models (0.5B-284B parameters, spanning text-only and vision-language architectures) and one closed frontier model, we find persistent trustworthiness gaps. Higher detection accuracy often coincides with greater demographic disparity, and models frequently comply with concealment or exaggeration prompts, assign high confidence to wrong predictions, rarely escalate ambiguous cases, and struggle to separate hate speech from counter-speech or reclaimed language (especially below 8B parameters). Abstract: Energy-based models (EBMs) assign a scalar energy to every joint value of the observed and predicted variables. In decision models, the prediction is chosen from a finite list of options provided with each input. Inference then reduces to comparing the energies of the options, and training lowers the energy of the correct option relative to the others. A complete decision must also account for the possibility that no option is acceptable. However, the energies learned by a standard EBM define only relative compatibility: adding the same input-dependent quantity to all energies leaves the predictions, the Gibbs distribution, and the usual training losses unchanged. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12980v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Spike cameras encode dynamic scenes into high-temporal-resolution binary spike streams for efficient high-speed vision. Although spiking neural networks (SNNs) can process such signals with sparse and accumulate-only computation, existing SNN-based reconstruction methods are typically shallow and still lag behind ANN-based models in reconstruction fidelity. This paper proposes MADSNet, a Multi-scale Axial-attentive Dense Spiking Network for spike camera image reconstruction. MADSNet adopts a hierarchical spiking encoder--decoder, where a multi-scale spike stem extracts early features, axial spike attention captures long-range dependencies, a dense spiking bottleneck enhances feature reuse, and a spike-to-continuous decoder reconstructs continuous intensity images from spike-domain representations. Experiments on gray-scale and color spike reconstruction show that MADSNet outperforms SSIR by 4.3 dB PSNR and Spk2ImgNet by 1.94 dB on SREDS.

Abstract: Generation, imputation, and prediction query different aspects of the same tabular distribution, but are usually evaluated separately. articles.title: Branch-and-Commit for Frozen RL Agents: When and Where to Spend Test-Time Compute
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13003v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reinforcement learning agents are often deployed with policies that cannot be retrained or modified. In digital environments whose states can be copied and resumed, an operator has another option: sample several continuations from the current state, evaluate them, and continue from the endpoint of the selected branch. We call this procedure branch-and-commit. We study when it improves return, what produces the improvement, and where its computational budget should be spent. Across four environments, two frozen policies, five continuation verifiers, and a model-free selection rule, we find that the benefit of branching depends on dispersion: the difference between the best candidate return and the mean candidate return. articles.title: The Shape of a Program: Path Signatures for Trace-to-Program Induction
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13005v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Synthesizing programs from execution traces is a fundamental challenge in algorithmic interpretability and the reverse engineering of complex systems. We bring a rough-path-theoretic perspective to program induction, treating execution traces as high-dimensional rough paths and encoding them with the path signature transform, a tool from stochastic analysis whose expectation provably characterizes the distribution of traces a program induces. On three program-induction domains, Karel, List, and RASP, our log-signature trace encoder outperforms LSTM, Transformer, and Fourier baselines in almost every setting, with its largest margins when training data is scarce. We further observe that the trace-to-program pipeline is naturally contractive: it often produces valid programs that are shorter than the ground truth. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13013v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Synthetic data augmentation promises to scale offline reinforcement learning beyond fixed logged datasets, but leading diffusion-based generators model the transition tuple (state, action, next state, reward, terminal) as a monolith: no single factor can be natively redrawn in isolation. Across twelve D4RL locomotion and maze benchmarks, TD3+BC and IQL agents trained on FaST transitions match the SynthER diffusion baseline while generating transitions over 90x faster. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13057v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Indoor localization commonly combines WiFi received signal strength indicator (RSSI) fingerprints with inertial measurements. However, these sensor streams are sampled asynchronously at different rates; therefore, observations rarely align in time and may be missing or stale. Most existing methods resample the data onto a shared clock and process each modality using a separate branch. We instead present a continuous-time transformer that represents observations as an unordered set of timestamped tokens. Each token encodes its measurement, modality, and elapsed time since acquisition. A single attention block jointly fuses information across modalities and time, avoiding both resampling and modality-specific branches while remaining invariant to token order. articles.content:

Abstract: Banks now train foundation models on ordered sequences of customer events such as transactions, app sessions, and authorizations. Deployed, such a model predicts forward in time, often for customers and merchants absent from training, yet each is evaluated on private data, so no two can be compared. Public benchmarks for such sequences rarely test a period the model has not seen; recommendation studies usually hold out each user's last events instead. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13070v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Brain networks exhibit modular organization, where community structures vary substantially across individuals and diseases. Understanding these individual differences is crucial for advancing both basic neuroscience research and precision medicine. However, widely used predefined group-level brain atlases often overlook this heterogeneity. While individualized functional parcellations capture subject-specific variability in community boundaries, they often require lengthy scan times to achieve fine-grained resolution and complicate cross-subject comparisons. Abstract: Inference-time sampling is a central mechanism for improving large language models, with temperature controlling the tradeoff between reliability and diversity. Abstract: Recent advancements in multimodal diffusion language models (MDLMs) have exhibited strong global modeling capabilities through iterative refinement. Abstract: Time series from real-world systems are often accompanied by text, such as a report on an event that affects them. Two common tasks on these series are understanding, e.g., answering questions about a series, and forecasting its future values. Both tasks require reasoning over the series and the text together. Moreover, understanding outputs text while forecasting outputs a time series, so serving both requires a model that reads and generates both modalities. Large language models (LLMs) read time series as digit tokens and handle long series poorly. Time series foundation models (TSFMs) forecast well from large-scale pretraining but typically neither read nor generate text. Time series language models add a time series modality to the LLM but forecast on the LLM side, leaving the TSFM's pretrained forecasting ability unused. articles.title: SELD: Detecting Silent Evidence Loss in Context Compression beyond the Answer
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12903v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Context compression is now routine for language models with long inputs, but a compressed context is useful only if it keeps the evidence for the answer. Existing checks compare the reader model's answer or its most likely words, and thus miss a frequent failure, silent evidence loss: key evidence is removed while the answer stays the same, leaving the answer unsupported and risky for other models that reuse the context. To address this challenge, we propose SELD (Silent Evidence Loss Detector), which needs no training and no labels. Its principle is that when evidence is lost, a reader model's preferences among the answers it leaves unsaid shift even if its answer does not, so comparing these preferences before and after compression reveals losses that answer checks cannot see. Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being deployed in clinical documentation workflows, where clinicians review and edit their outputs before use. articles.title: Capacity Allocation at the Source: Sparse Target Optimization for LLM Knowledge Editing
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12995v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Knowledge editing has emerged as a promising approach for efficiently updating embedded knowledge in large language models (LLMs). It first computes an ideal target hidden state that steers the LLM toward the new output, and then edits the model parameters so that the original hidden state is mapped to this target. While most existing methods focus on the second stage of parameter editing in preserving other knowledge, we find that the upstream construction of the target hidden state also plays an important role in allocating the model's limited capacity space. We first establish a theoretical connection between interference in the parameter space and interference between target hidden states, showing that the two are positively correlated. Building on this insight, we propose a simple yet effective $\ell_1$ regularization method that prunes away unnecessary ``tentacles'' of each knowledge vector, retaining only the essential components.

Abstract: Thai is written without spaces between words, making segmentation a foundational step in most Thai NLP pipelines. Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly trusted with mathematical, scientific and engineering work, yet their mistakes are often confidently written and hard to spot. Abstract: Cultural adaptation in dialogue systems refers to the ability to generate responses that conform to linguistic norms and social expectations across different cultures. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13223v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reasoning models write a reasoning trace at every turn of a multi-turn tool session, and later turns read this history. Across 94k ShareGPT conversations, 73 percent of user interactions span multiple turns. Abstract: Recent work has identified a set of emergent symbolic mechanisms that support abstract reasoning in large language models, but it remains unclear what factors drive the emergence of these mechanisms. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13339v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In social science research, text annotation is a fundamental task that is traditionally a costly, hard-to-scale manual process. Researchers have used large language models (LLMs) to perform annotation by writing a definition of a concept into a prompt - a rule that determines whether a label should be attributed to a text depending on its content. However, concepts such as hate speech, fake news, and terrorism typically have several theoretically defensible competing definitions. It is also unknown whether the model actually applied the definition to provide the label or the label was based on the model's pretrained notion of the concept. articles.title: Understanding Students' Rationales for AI-Mediated Cheating: An Instructor Perspective from Online Forums Analysis
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13358v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The extensive adoption of AI has precipitated a crisis in academic integrity. While studies attempt to quantify cheating, less is known about the motivations instructors believe students have for using AI in prohibited ways. We analyze 2.01 million posts on r/Professors to understand how instructors perceive students' justifications for AI-mediated cheating. Our qualitative analyses reveal four primary themes: (1) Academic System Gaming, (2) Digital-Academic Literacy Gap, (3) Performance Anxiety, and (4) Normalization of Dishonesty.

Abstract: Most language models deployed outside the United States and China are fine-tuned descendants of a small number of pretrained families. Abstract: Reconstructing high-fidelity LiDAR simulation scenes from real-world driving logs is essential for cost-effective safety validation of autonomous driving systems. Abstract: Open-vocabulary object detection (OVD) expects the model trained on base classes to recognize both base and novel classes at inference. Typical methods rely on CLIP-style vision-language embeddings, yet the learned space is often biased toward base categories, with limited effective capacity preserved for novel concepts. Such a base-dominated representation can compress novel semantics, leading to semantic collapse and mis-calibrated confidence at inference. To address this issue, we present PR-OVD, a partition-and-refine framework that explicitly reserves capacity for novel categories and strengthens category separation, while being seamlessly integrated into different detector architectures. Abstract: Surgical action-center localization requires both an accurate reference point and a decision about whether to report it. articles.title: Trajectory-Regularized Distribution Distillation for One-Step Generation
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12978v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Distilling flow matching models for one-step generation generally follows two paradigms. Trajectory alignment supervises the student with the teacher's probability flow ODE, but its performance degrades under very small sampling budgets. Distribution matching directly optimizes the generated distribution, but estimating its reverse Kullback-Leibler gradient typically requires a separate network to track the evolving student score. We propose trajectory-regularized distribution distillation (TRD), which combines distribution-level and trajectory-level supervision through a momentum-mixture policy predicted in a single student forward pass. This policy serves simultaneously as a one-step generator, an estimator of the student's marginal velocity that removes the need for a second trainable network in distribution matching, and a closed-form time-dependent velocity field supervised along the teacher ODE trajectory. Abstract: Overlapping imaging manifestations complicate the differential diagnosis of Diffuse Cystic Lung Diseases (DCLDs), while limited annotated data constrain supervised model development. Abstract: Multimodal (e.g. vision-language, in this work) attribution aims to interpret the models without access to ground-truth explanatory supervision. Abstract: Discrete autoregressive models offer a scalable framework for image generation. Abstract: Complete-or-reject reporting of surgical action triplets can discard a correctly identified instrument and action when the target is uncertain. Abstract: Graphical user interface (GUI) grounding maps a screenshot and a natural-language instruction to the screen location where an agent should act. Zoomed views can reveal small targets but may lose the context needed to identify them. We introduce GroundCascade, a training-free controller that uses agreement between a grounder's full-screen and zoomed predictions to decide when to consult a complementary model. It selects between zoomed predictions while preserving corroborated full-screen locations. An optional Finalizer predicts from an unmarked joint crop when disagreement remains (Full); omitting it yields the two-stage Selective variant. articles.title: Maze Runner: Autonomous Maze Navigation with Line-Based Localization and Control Barrier Functions
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12949v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Maze navigation requires localization from sparse, repetitive geometry, planning through narrow corridors, and control that stays safe when the estimate or the map is wrong. We present Maze Runner, an open autonomy stack in C++ and ROS 2 that addresses these needs end to end on a simulated Husarion ROSbot XL with a 2D LiDAR in Gazebo. Perception extracts wall lines from each scan with RANSAC and total least squares, with per-line uncertainty. The same line front end feeds two estimators: an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) that localizes against a line map built from the maze mesh, and an EKF SLAM variant that builds the line map online. Planning runs online on an inflated occupancy grid with A* plus line-of-sight shortcutting, or with a forward-only Hybrid A*. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12983v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Scene-driven robot autonomy requires selecting tasks from observations as well as executing them. We study scene-driven task formulation and execution under predefined cleaning, safety, and storage/organization categories, without instance-specific goals or action sequences. CAFE maintains online memory of objects, functional zones, and execution states. A rule-guided Trigger-LLM admits formulation from accumulated evidence; Draft, Complete, and Audit propose goals, resolve execution details, and check dependencies. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13034v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Robot agents can improve reusable skills, planning procedures, and recovery strategies from execution feedback, yet a fixed practice source leaves the search for new weaknesses unchanged. Useful practice depends on the agent's current capabilities, so the procedure that chooses practice must also be revisable. We present RoboACE (Robot Adversarial Co-Evolution), a framework that jointly evolves curriculum and execution harnesses around frozen foundation models. The curriculum harness uses accumulated capability evidence to propose informative challenges, while the execution harness responds with reusable revisions that expand execution capabilities. Alternating updates hold one side fixed as the other changes, and admitted challenges form fixed snapshots for comparing execution revisions. articles.title: Robo-MLT: Dual-System Robotic Manipulation for Long-Horizon Medical Laboratory Tasks
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13039v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reliable medical laboratory automation requires robots to complete entire workflows in protocol order while handling changes during execution. A robot may execute each motion correctly yet fail the workflow by confusing visually similar stages or stalling after human intervention. We present Robo-MLT, a dual-system framework that couples explicit workflow monitoring with learned action generation. A vision--language planner composes an ordered atomic-skill sequence from the protocol and the initial workspace observation. A multiframe execution monitor detects when the active skill has completed or become infeasible, then advances the workflow or triggers replanning. A skill-conditioned vision--language--action policy generates the manipulation trajectories, and an asynchronous runtime coordinates it with the monitor. articles.title: ASPIRE: An Agentic System-Identification Platform for Iterative Reasoning and Exploration
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13114v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: System identification requires expert decisions on the identification method, incorporation of prior physical knowledge, and model validation. We propose ASPIRE, a framework for nonlinear system identification in which a large language model agent selects and executes the identification method. ASPIRE constructs closed-form, nonlinear static or dynamic models from measured data, optionally supplemented by a system description, the intended use of the model, and physical requirements expressed formally or in natural language. Each model includes its parameters, an estimation record, an interpretation of its terms, and an error evaluated on test data inaccessible to the agent. Formal physical requirements are verified independently. ASPIRE operates autonomously or interactively, allowing the agent to ask questions and the user to request further analyses and identification rounds. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13142v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Learning-based decentralized collision avoidance must remain reliable under state-estimation uncertainty and heterogeneous agent dynamics. Existing methods typically address these factors through training-domain variation or by exposing uncertainty and capability estimates to the policy at runtime. However, both leave the policy to infer how these quantities should alter the physical separation required for safe interaction, which can couple collision-avoidance behavior to relationships learned from the training distribution. We introduce the Dynamic Oriented Bounding Box (DOBB), an online geometric representation that maps the current state estimate, uncertainty, and agent-specific response characteristics into a dynamic, direction-dependent safety margin. Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models now exceed 95% success on the LIBERO simulation benchmark, yet it remains unclear how much of this performance requires generalization beyond the training demonstrations. In this work, we show that retrieving nearby demonstrations and reusing their action chunks achieves a success rate of 91.7 % on LIBERO without policy training. Under LIBERO-Plus perturbations, retrieval shows the smallest drop of all evaluated policies. Across nine publicly available VLAs, fine-tuning mostly makes the vision-language backbone a better retrieval key, and the actions of the VLAs remain close to the demonstrations. articles.title: Ground Reaction Force-Aware Model Predictive Control for Underactuated Upright Physical Assistance
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13204v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Many rehabilitation robots execute prescribed motions using reactive tracking controllers that do not explicitly incorporate the user's instantaneous human-ground interaction. This paper presents Ground Reaction Force-Aware Model Predictive Control (GRF-MPC), a framework for upright physical assistance. By integrating live GRF and center of pressure (CoP) measurements directly into a human centroidal dynamics model, GRF-MPC formulates a real-time quadratic program (QP) that optimizes assistive forces and moments over a receding horizon. We deployed GRF-MPC on the Robotic Upright Stand Trainer (RobUST) in an underactuated 4-cable configuration and evaluated it against a fully actuated 8-cable Cartesian impedance baseline in nearly 300 trials across six healthy participants. Across tasks spanning impulsive perturbations, lunge trajectories, and voluntary limits of stability, GRF-MPC reduced peak planar center-of-mass (CoM) error by 19.6% d

articles.title: Latent Barrier Steering: Hierarchical Safety for Generative Planning
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13227v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We introduce Latent Barrier Steering (LBS), a hierarchical semantic-to-path framework for safe flow-matching-based generative planning. Existing control-barrier-function (CBF) safety filters for diffusion and flow-matching planners act locally on generated samples, either during sampling or after prediction. Such repair is effective for small violations, but can struggle when a new constraint blocks the whole selected behavior mode rather than merely perturbing it locally. LBS decouples behavior selection from path certification through two coordinated interventions: it first steers the generator's behavior latent toward rollouts with larger safety margin, then decodes the steered latent and applies a path-space CBF quadratic program (QP) only for residual violations. We show that latent steering increases the margin available to the path-space corrector, yielding finite-time recovery guarantees and reduced correction burden. Experiments

articles.title: Incorporating World Models in Decision Making for Next Best View Selection in Active Sensing
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13229v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Efficient robotic 3D reconstruction requires selecting views that contribute new surface measurements with few physical captures. Pretrained world models can guide this choice, but a predicted surface may not produce valid depth measurements under the operating conditions of the deployed sensor. We present a deployment adaptation methodology for next-best-view selection that learns a sensor-return adapter from limited local calibration data while keeping the pretrained predictor fixed. The adapter estimates measurement dropout over each predicted surface, allowing the selection method to favor views likely to fill gaps in the measured reconstruction. In a real-robot experiment with a structured-light sensor, the adapted method achieves higher measured surface coverage with 60% fewer captures than nominal selection. articles.title: Curie's Jarvis: Autonomous Robotic Chemistry Experiments from Printed Protocols
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13251v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A person running a bench experiment works from a printed instruction sheet, tells identical containers apart by the labels written on them, and looks at the bench again before each step. Lab automation usually works the other way around: the procedure is written as a script, and containers stand at fixed positions or carry fiducial markers. We present Curie's Jarvis, a system that lets a robot arm carry out a chemistry experiment on a bench set up for people. It reads the steps from a photo of the printed sheet, finds containers on an ordinary bench with no fixed positions or markers, tells identical-looking containers apart by reading their labels in four camera views, locates its target again before every step, and sets how each step is carried out, including its speed, from what is being handled. articles.title: Force-Closure Condition for Cooperative Multi-robot Pushing of Rectangular Objects
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13268v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In cooperative object manipulation, the placement of pushing contacts determines whether force closure can be achieved and agents can generate arbitrary forces and torques on the object correspondingly. This study derives a necessary and sufficient closed-form condition for the planar force closure of a rectangular object, a common object shape in everyday settings, under four frictionless pushing contacts. For a rectangle of length $b$ and width $a$, force closure holds if and only if $(l_1+l_3-b)(l_2+l_4-a)<0$, where $l_1,l_2,l_3,l_4$ are the four edge contact locations. This condition is independent of the object's center of mass and is used to verify contact configurations before contact force allocation. When the condition is not satisfied, the signs of the two factors indicate which opposing contact pair should be adjusted. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13271v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar provides weather-robust sensing and direct Doppler measurements, yet automotive perception pipelines often reduce its output to sparse point clouds or two-dimensional projections, leaving raw range-azimuth-Doppler (RAD) cubes underutilized. Ego motion induces Doppler responses from world-static structures, while Doppler wrapping aliases radial velocities, complicating moving-object detection and velocity estimation. articles.title: Large Language Model Explainability for Planning Lunar Rover Trajectories under Uncertainty
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13292v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Planning planetary rover trajectories under probabilistic uncertainty is a multi-objective optimization problem that science teams currently iteratively solve and verify by hand. This process becomes impractical when timelines and constraints frequently shift throughout the mission planning phase. Sampling-based planners such as Monte Carlo tree search can speed up this process, but their outputs do not preserve traceability to the science objectives that justify each plan, which the science team needs to verify. We propose an interactive assistant based on a large language model (LLM) that can explain planner trajectories using domain vocabulary and re-run the planner under user-specified conditions to compare alternatives. Abstract: Task-driven design of soft robots requires the consideration of factors such as geometry, morphology, material properties, and actuation, resulting in a large and complex design space that is challenging to explore. Computational optimisation methods leverage signals from simulation to iteratively improve designs to achieve task objectives. articles.title: AHEADance: Anticipatory Humanoid Dance from Streaming Audio
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13370v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A humanoid that dances to streamed music must commit each motion chunk before it has heard the music that chunk accompanies, and must continue from motion it has already committed. We present AHEADance, a robot-native streaming dance generator executed on a humanoid robot by a whole-body tracker. ListenAhead conditions each chunk on heard music and a frozen music model's forecasts of the coming music, aligned to their target times and weighted by reliability. The forecasts carry the timing of upcoming beats almost as well as the actual future; with them, the generator is better synchronized with the music and concentrates more motion energy at its song's beat frequency. Commit Forcing trains continuation from the model's own committed chunks, updating both the latent history and the decoded boundary of the next chunk; it reduces low activity from 83.5% to 10.3%, the level of real dance. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13382v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Decision making in multi-agent and multi-robot systems often involves discrete decision variables, leading to NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems that must be solved within seconds for near real-time implementation. Denoising diffusion has emerged as a powerful tool for such problems, but existing approaches face a trade-off: Model-Based Diffusion (MBD) incorporates diffusion in sampling-based optimization (SBO) without training but only over continuous spaces, while existing diffusion-based combinatorial solvers operate over discrete spaces but require offline training. To this end, we propose Discrete Model-Based Diffusion (Discrete MBD), a training-free SBO method that directly optimizes discrete variables by approximating categorical reverse transition distributions through Monte Carlo sampling. articles.title: Rhythmic-Semantic Co-Speech Gestures for Emotional Dialogue in Robots
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13472v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Co-speech gestures can increase engagement and improve speech understanding. Yet, most data-driven robot systems generate either rhythmic beat-like motion or semantically meaningful iconic gestures, but not both. We present an emotion-aware rhythmic-semantic co-speech gesture system that generates iconic and beat behaviors in real time from text and the robot's internal emotional state. We formalize the task of beat-iconic gesture generation using emotion and propose lightweight models that predict iconic timing and intensity, then fill the remaining spans with emotion-conditioned beats at an appropriate intensity level. We train on the BEAT2 dataset and deploy the system on the social robot Haru. In an online user study with 60 participants, our method shows stronger speech-gesture alignment and is preferred over baseline methods.

articles.title: Medical Image Segmentation: Foundation Model Adaptation versus Task-Specific Training
articles.content: Foundation models pretrained on large natural-image collections are increasingly adapted for medical image segmentation, in the expectation that they will replace models trained for each task. Most comparisons, however, use data from the training distribution and a single task-specific baseline whose configuration is rarely justified, and therefore provide limited evidence of performance at new clinical sites. It also remains unclear how much of a foundation model must be adapted, and what determines this. We adapted a foundation model, DINOv2, with strategies ranging from tuning only its bias terms to full fine-tuning, and compared it with U-Nets and ResU-Nets trained from scratch. Experiments covered colonoscopy, breast ultrasound and dermoscopy, with testing on held-out data from the training source and on independent datasets from other institutions. The adapted foundation model generalised better on every external dataset. Within the training distribution, the task-specific models remained competitive when training data were abundant, and delineated boundaries more precisely, while the foundation model more often missed small lesions. Only a small fraction of the foundation model required adaptation, and the capacity needed was determined by the imaging domain rather than by the adaptation method. A widely used polyp test set was also found to duplicate images from another benchmark. Foundation-model adaptation is therefore warranted where models must work across sites, with capacity selected on the target domain.

articles.title: Toward Foundation Detection Models via Example-Based Grounding in EM-DETR
articles.content: DeepLearning (DL)-based Computer-Aided Diagnostic (CAD) systems have shown great promise in supporting clinicians, but their performance heavily depends on the availability of large, well-annotated datasets. In medical lesion detection, the scarcity of comprehensive, stan dardized annotations and the heterogeneity of existing datasets limit the development of robust foundation models. In this work, we introduce a novel approach to building a multi-domain foundation model for le sion detection by integrating diverse medical image datasets annotated for both anatomical structures and abnormalities. We first propose a student-teacher training strategy to effectively combine datasets with heterogeneous label spaces, mitigating catastrophic forgetting, and im proving feature learning. In addition, building on our previously pro posed example-based EM-DETR framework, we adapt it to jointly learn from multiple domain-specific datasets, enabling fine-grained, example driven detection across modalities. Our model achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) results, with image-level AUC scores exceeding previous SOTA by 1% point on four key findings in CXRs. We achieve a leading mAP50 in CXRs and mammography, surpassing EM-DETR trained on a single dataset by 2-3% points. This approach paves the way for scalable foundation models in medical imaging that leverage heterogeneous data while maintaining robust and generalizable performance.

articles.title: TorchCurves: Differentiable Parametric Curves
articles.content: We present TorchCurves, a PyTorch library that treats vector-valued parametric curves as learnable primitives. Its central operation maps batches of scalar inputs to points on curves represented in B-spline or Legendre polynomial bases, with differentiation through both inputs and coefficients. Curve coefficients can be optimized jointly with the surrounding model or produced by another network. The library provides trainable modules, reusable basis modules, and a functional interface, supporting applications ranging from continuous feature embeddings to Kolmogorov-Arnold networks and functional regression. Its implementation combines classical evaluation algorithms with vectorized PyTorch operations, emphasizing readability and maintainability without custom hardware kernels. Timing experiments compare curve evaluation against NumPy and SciPy and KAN training against EfficientKAN across a range of problem sizes. The results illustrate where this generality remains computationally practical and where overhead is substantial. Library is available on GitHub at https://github.com/alexshtf/torchcurves.

articles.title: AutoScaffold: AI-Guided Scaffolding for Reinforcement Learning of Language Models
articles.content: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) produces rich training experience, yet outcome rewards reduce each attempt to a single number and leave most of this information unused. Training-time scaffolds, such as strategies or hints added to the prompt during training, offer a natural way to turn this information into guidance, but their design and adaptation are largely left to humans and tailored to specific domains. We introduce AutoScaffold, a unified AI-for-AI framework that turns a student's training experience into adaptive scaffolds, with minimal domain-specific information and no human intervention during training. A frozen teacher periodically examines this experience, diagnoses bottlenecks, and designs scaffolds in two forms: (i) strategies shared across a class of tasks and (ii) hints for individual hard tasks, adjusting the content and amount of support as the student learns. The scaffolds are removed at evaluation. We apply the same framework to ALFWorld, search-based QA, mathematical reasoning, and GPU kernel generation. When evaluated without scaffolds, students trained with AutoScaffold outperform those trained with the corresponding RL baselines in all four domains, with gains of 7.2 points in ALFWorld success and 4.0 points in average QA exact match. On GPU kernel generation, AutoScaffold increases the fraction of tasks with a correct kernel that runs faster than the PyTorch reference by up to 5.0 points. On math, our student surpasses QuestA's reported accuracy using approximately one-third as many student training steps. Analyses show that the teacher identifies a different failure in each task class and shifts its scaffolds from step-by-step workflows to targeted fixes as the student improves, and that its revised scaffolds help the student learn more than keeping the previous scaffold or using no scaffold.

articles.title: Contrastive Discovery: Open-Ended Scientific Discovery over Competing Explanations
articles.content: LLM agents are increasingly used for open-ended, data-driven scientific discovery, yet most of them evaluate hypotheses pointwise, testing an empirical claim $h$ only against its complement $\neg h$. When evidence rejects $h$, the agent learns that one explanation is unlikely but not which alternative the evidence supports. To recover that alternative, we introduce Contrastive Discovery, which replaces the single hypothesis with a contrast set, a scientific question paired with mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive competing explanations. Each experiment is scored by how its evidence redistributes belief across the set, and the question is resolved when belief concentrates on one explanation. Because contrast sets change only the unit an agent proposes and scores, an existing agent can use them to re-evaluate evidence it has already collected or to guide its search. Across six domains, $89\%$ of the pointwise candidates with the largest belief shifts are rejections. On the same evidence, contrast sets resolve $73\%$ of these candidates to a specific alternative. When contrast sets guide search, the agent resolves $67\%$ more questions than pointwise surprisal under the same experiment budget. In a blinded study, $38$ human experts chose the same explanation on $78\%$ of resolved questions and on $82\%$ of questions where the pointwise agent rejected its hypothesis and stopped. Together, these results support explicit competing explanations as a way for discovery agents to resolve more scientific questions from the same evidence and validation budget.

articles.title: Pyrite: Building and Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking Agents
articles.content: Predicting how a ligand binds to its target is central to small-molecule drug discovery. Modern cofolding models can generate diverse candidate poses, but reliably ranking these candidates remains challenging. We introduce Pyrite, a pairwise pose-ranking benchmark comprising 1,500 pose pairs across diverse protein-ligand complexes. Expert chemists equipped with 3D visualization tools and physics-based scores perform near chance, highlighting the difficulty of interpreting available chemical signals. To investigate automated ranking, we introduce PyriteRep, a structured representation of molecular geometry, protein-ligand interactions, and physicochemical scores, and develop two LLM-based agents: PyriteReasoner, which directly compares poses through text-based reasoning, and PyriteFeaturizer, which generates executable code to construct features for logistic regression, optionally incorporating features derived from LLM subcalls. These agents achieve up to 67% and 74% accuracy, respectively, exceeding observed expert performance. LLM-guided feature discovery generally outperforms direct reasoning, while Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) improves open-weight models, enabling them to match or surpass closed-source frontier models in our evaluations. These results establish Pyrite as a challenging test of pose-ranking ability and highlight LLM-guided feature discovery as a promising approach to interpret and combine the outputs of computational chemistry tools.

articles.title: When Does the Real Wiring Win? Testing connectome structure-function claims against unmeasured physiology
articles.content: Connectome-constrained models are often used to argue that a measured wiring diagram outperforms shuffled or rewired wiring, and hence that structure shapes function. Such comparisons can confound wiring with how the models are tuned: a connectome fixes who connects to whom, not the excitability, gains or plasticity rates the model also needs, and modellers often tune these until the real-wiring model works. We separate three estimands: physiology tuned on the real wiring and transferred to nulls (P1), each wiring tuned on its own (P2), and P2 restricted to physiology consistent with independent data (P3). The biases involved are known in machine learning (under-tuned baselines, inherited weights, winner's curse); we measure what they do to biological conclusions, using synthetic ground truth, placebo nulls and three Drosophila circuit models. Some claims survive every protocol we test: segregated reward and punishment dopamine improves learning, and head-direction topography is required for a persistent bump. Others do not. In the mushroom body, the real Kenyon-cell output wiring beats a cross-subtype identity shuffle by 0.09 under P1 and P2 but loses to it by 0.09 under P3 (95% CIs exclude zero; held-out runs confirm). The verdict is set by the share of alpha'beta' cells among active Kenyon cells, which P1 selects low; at the share implied by imaging (about 44%) the real-wiring model fails to learn, exposing a model inadequacy rather than a deficit of the fly's wiring. In flyvis, P1 penalises a mirrored connectome, which has a constructed solution within 0.07 (median) of the real error, more than a spatially shuffled one in 50 of 50 members; the ranking survives ten-fold longer retraining but depends on the checkpoint at fifty-fold. A credible structural claim needs matched optimisation, data-constrained physiology and a model that still works there.

articles.title: Continual-ARC: Measuring Skill Acquisition over a Working Lifetime
articles.content: Agent harnesses have emerged as a promising mechanism for continual learning, alongside test-time parametric learning. However, the current benchmarks have several limitations: they generally focus on a single applied domain, serve each instance only once, and assume a single family of learner, so memory-based and weight-based systems are rarely compared on the same scale. We propose Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream built from the three ARC-AGI editions, whose tasks need no domain knowledge. The same tasks return after dormant gaps with fresh instances, while new tasks keep arriving. On each instance, the learner may pay for demonstrations, submit answers, or act inside the harness, with retries permitted on incorrect submissions, which are paid for. Each instance is scored based on the share of this feedback budget consumed. Since a learner may keep anything between instances, memory-based and weight-based systems are scored on the same scale. After the stream, the learner is frozen and tested on fresh instances of the tasks it met, which measures memorization, and on unseen tasks, which measures generalization. We run an agent harness with frozen weights, with and without persistence, on Qwen3.5-9B and GLM-5.3 Flash, comparing them with two prompting floors, a program-induction method and Qwen3.5-9B's weights trained to imitate GLM-5.3 Flash. Persistence in the harness generally does not improve memorization unless provided with explicit expert guidance. Most harness-based methods still learn less than a floor that simply caches each task's demonstrations, across all models we tested. No harness-based method gains on unseen tasks, whereas weight-based learning shows substantial gains. This opens the door to future weight-based continual learning that could teach models to drive harnesses in new domains.

articles.title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions
articles.content: Foundation models trained on large unlabeled corpora develop emergent capabilities, tasks that go beyond the training objective. We extend this paradigm to multimodal biology with Bonbon, a foundation model for molecular interactions trained on approximately 3.2 trillion tokens of paired protein-ligand sequences. From a single representation space, Bonbon exhibits three zero-shot emergent capabilities at hierarchical levels of resolution: functional (mechanism of action), residue (binding site localization, including orthosteric/allosteric discrimination), and bond (covalent versus non-covalent engagement). All three capabilities generalize to out-of-distribution complexes. Bonbon was trained on protein-ligand sequences alone, without any task-specific supervision and without structural coordinates. We conducted controlled scaling experiments across six model scales from 42M to 1.6B parameters; every capability evaluated shows a sharp jump at the largest scale on continuous metrics, even as pretraining loss decreases smoothly. This demonstrates that loss-based scaling laws alone are insufficient to predict when zero-shot emergent capabilities become available. The capabilities reported here emerge after training at a 1:2,000 parameter-to-token ratio to accommodate the sparsity of paired biological interaction data. The same frozen representations achieve state-of-the-art binding and affinity prediction at five orders of magnitude greater speed than co-folding methods. In prospective wet-lab validation across nine disease targets spanning seven protein families, Bonbon achieves a 61.5% dose-response hit rate on de novo compounds, yielding structurally novel molecules not previously reported to inhibit these proteins, including for out-of-distribution targets.

articles.title: Measuring Robustness and Efficiency in a Connectome-Constrained Fly Visual System Model: Linking an Adversarial and a Perceptual Illusion
articles.content: Biological visual systems compute reliably under tight metabolic and wiring constraints, whereas artificial vision systems consume far more energy and can be sensitive to adversarial perturbations. Whether networks with brain-like wiring are more robust at lower computational cost is unclear. We address this by benchmarking a task-optimized, continuous-time recurrent neural network of the fly visual system constrained by its synaptic connectome (FlyNet) against artificial neural networks. We compare it against CNNs, RAFT, and continuous-time recurrent neural networks without detailed connectome constraints (sCTRNN, CTRNN) on a collision-detection task within a differentiable 3D rendering pipeline. FlyNet is adversarially vulnerable but, relative to its compute, more robust to common video corruptions than RAFT, while using up to five orders of magnitude fewer FLOPs. The CTRNNs remain more robust than FlyNet across almost all tested perturbations, suggesting that connectome constraints benefit efficiency, through their low edge count, over robustness. Recurrence improves robustness to white-box attacks in RAFT and temporal context improves robustness to common corruptions. FlyNet's position and velocity representations degrade under adversarial textures but recover under counterfactual textures that restore correct classification while staying equally far from training, ruling out unfamiliar textures as the cause of failure. The reverse-phi illusion similarly disrupts these representations and inverts the same low-level motion statistic as the adversarial textures. Optimizing this input statistic alone, without access to the network, suffices to induce classification failure, attributing both perturbations to the same circuit vulnerability. Connectome-constrained models can thus surface adversarial failure mechanisms as testable hypotheses about biological perceptual vulnerabilities.

articles.title: RS-JEPA: Remote Sensing Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture with Scan-Path Views for Cross-Sensor Image Retrieval
articles.content: Cross-sensor remote sensing image retrieval aims to find scenes with the same content across heterogeneous sensors, such as SAR and optical or panchromatic (PAN) and multispectral (MS) imagery, without manual labels. Existing self-supervised methods either reconstruct sensor-specific pixel detail, align each image only with its co-registered twin, or rely on large transformers with 118-173M parameters (and up to 398M). We introduce RS-JEPA, a compact joint-embedding predictive framework built on a Vision Mamba encoder shared by both sensors. Since a state-space encoder reads an image as an ordered sequence of patches, we propose scan-path views, which treat two reading orders of the same image as two views with identical pixels and predict the hidden patches in one order from the visible patches in the other.To keep this prediction challenging, we propose Adversarial View Coupling (AVC), which learns the hardest split of the visible patches, and a neighbourhood consensus loss that aligns the scene similarities of both sensors. Extensive experiments on SAR-optical (BEN-14K, CBRSIR-VS) and PAN-MS (DSRSID) benchmarks demonstrate that RS-JEPA achieves the highest F1@5 among twelve re-implemented methods (72.92, 80.35 and 94.43) with a retrieval network of only 3.88M parameters (14.57M in training, 8-16times fewer than prior JEPA retrievers). Like prior methods, RS-JEPA trains on co-registered pairs. Our results highlight reading order as a source of self-supervised views. code: https://github.com/Tanishq251/RSJEPA.

articles.title: Comparative Analysis of Agent Evaluation Frameworks: Stability, Detection, and Discovery in Enterprise Analytics Agents
articles.content: Deploying LLM-based analytics agents in enterprise settings requires evaluation frameworks that can reliably detect failures across complex, multi-tool workflows. We present a three-phase comparative study of three evaluation frameworks, each representing a distinct evaluation paradigm (trace-based LLM judging, text-only LLM judging with red-teaming, and deterministic heuristics), applied to two analytics agents in a controlled research setting using frozen execution traces. Phase 1 quantifies evaluation harness stability through repeated measurements, finding that 97% of configurations meet the stability threshold and that stability patterns are agent-independent. Phase 2 measures known risk detection on 72 ground-truth test cases, where the trace-based framework achieves the best precision-recall balance (F1=0.90) while text-only evaluation matches on recall but generates 5x more false alarms. Phase 3 evaluates unknown risk discovery, uncovering 24 novel failures with zero overlap between functional testing and security red-teaming. Our results demonstrate that (1) the information available to the evaluation harness determines evaluation quality, (2) functional and security evaluation are complementary, and (3) LLM-based evaluation harnesses surface subtle errors that human reviewers miss. We recommend a two-framework strategy: trace-based evaluation for functional assessment and adversarial red-teaming for security validation.

articles.title: ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows
articles.content: Business process automation runs the same Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) again and again on new inputs. Large Language Model (LLM) agents can follow an SOP written in natural language, but they call an LLM to choose every step of every run, which adds latency and cost at scale. We present ReTrace, which turns an SOP and a few logged agent runs into a reusable workflow in which code, not an LLM, selects the next step. The agent's reasoning, the explanation it writes with each tool call, often states why it took an action; the tool calls alone do not. ReTrace extracts the condition behind each step, merges these conditions across runs into a compact rule document, and generates an executable workflow from it. Only this last stage depends on the platform, so rule documents can be compiled for different orchestration platforms. On $79$ procedures from our production platform, ReTrace workflows reach $93.8\%$ completion, against $96.8\%$ for the agent, at $24\%$ lower cost per task. On $τ^2$-Bench, they reach $75.8\%$ task success (agent: $80.6\%$) and run in $1.3$s instead of $170$s; three rounds of repair on training failures lift $k{=}2$ workflows from $66.7\%$ to $81.2\%$. On eight SOP-Bench procedures, ReTrace without repair trails few-shot generation ($80.6\%$ vs. $83.6\%$), but repair from labeled training failures lifts it to $87.8\%$ at $0.40$s per task, compared to $85.5\%$ in $46.6$s for the agent.

articles.title: TimeSeek: Multi-Task and Multi-Domain Pretraining for Generalized Time Series Analytics
articles.content: Time series analytics has been widely applied across various domains. While existing time series foundation models (TSFMs) have demonstrated promising results, they still face two major challenges: 1) Most TSFMs mainly rely on stacking Transformer layers to increase parameter size, lacking the ability to adaptively model complex time series patterns from multi-domain data. 2) Current TSFMs are primarily pre-trained for specific tasks, e.g., forecasting or anomaly detection, and a few models support multiple tasks, but they fail to fully leverage task specificity and commonality, resulting in suboptimal performance. To address these challenges, we propose TimeSeek, a novel generalized time series analytics model that adaptively models time series patterns from multi-domain data and unifies multiple tasks in pre-training. Conceptually, TimeSeek is guided by selective information sharing under domain and task heterogeneity. From the perspective of multi-domain data, we propose a Multi-Domain Feature Extractor that adaptively captures temporal dependencies and channel correlations based on domain-specific characteristics, including progressive multi-scale modeling and adaptive slot channel modeling. From the perspective of the diversity of tasks, we propose multi-task collaborative training, which leverages task specificity and task commonality through task customization and cross-task training, effectively unifying multiple tasks in pre-training and better adapting to diverse downstream scenarios. After pre-training on large-scale time series data, TimeSeek achieves state-of-the-art performance in forecasting, anomaly detection, and classification tasks across both few-shot learning and zero-shot situations, together with favorable inference efficiency.

articles.title: Is Your Robot's Memory Just a Clock? Temporal Shortcuts in Memory-Augmented VLA Policies
articles.content: Memory-augmented vision-language-action (VLA) policies are meant to remember what happened. Many of them, however, fill memory by time: they sample frames uniformly across the episode and stamp each frame with its time step. Because time passes even when nothing happens, such a memory may not tell waiting from working. We show that it does not. On the counting tasks of RoboMME, we make the robot briefly pause or fidget its wrist. Such a null event changes nothing the task depends on, yet a released memory VLA counts the interval as work done and stops early. We call this failure phantom progress. It cuts success from 47 to 16 of 50 on one task and from 44 to 10 on the other. When the same frames are withheld from memory, success returns, so the cause lies in memory rather than in the interruption itself. We trace the failure to a temporal shortcut: because demonstrations proceed at a steady pace, elapsed time predicts progress. Indeed, rescaling the time stamps alone makes the policy stop early when the clock runs fast and repeat when it runs slow. Surprisingly, removing the time encoding does not cure the failure, because the frames of a null event still occupy slots of the time-sampled memory. Across RoboMME's released designs, vulnerability follows how memory is indexed. Of the fixes the diagnosis suggests, training with injected pauses does not remove the failure and impairs counting, whereas indexing memory by events recovers half or more of the loss without retraining. A memory meant to remember what happened should count events rather than clock ticks.

articles.title: Re-Search: Dissecting LLM Ideation Through a Two-Player Questioning Game
articles.content: Research ideation is iterative: researchers refine their ideas step by step based on feedback. Yet existing evaluations obscure this search process, making it difficult to understand how LLMs explore the space of research ideas and what limits their progress. We introduce Re-Search, which adapts the format of Twenty Questions to research ideation: given only the research problem of a published paper, a model must rediscover the paper's core idea by asking yes-or-no questions. Built from 200 ICML 2026 papers, Re-Search tracks how a model's idea evolves as it asks questions and receives binary oracle feedback, isolating ideation from execution. Across six recent LLMs, nearly all progress happens within the first 30 of 100 questions, which largely decide how the game ends; after that, most models plateau. Through controlled interventions on the candidate questions and the hypothesis space, we find that the bottleneck is generation, not judgment: models recognize a good idea or a good question when one is offered, but often cannot produce it on their own. We further analyze the ideation traces and find that models fail by either over-exploiting one direction or over-exploring too many. These findings point to concrete design principles for autoresearch systems: since models can judge candidates they cannot produce, enriching the search with externally sourced ideas and questions may be more effective than improving any single model's generation ability.
